biography.currentRole: Private citizen; former U.S. Representative, TX-34 (June 2022 – January 2023, 117th Congress)
priorRoles: U.S. Representative TX-34, 117th Congress (June 21, 2022 – Jan 3, 2023) — won June 2022 special election, lost November 2022 general to Vicente Gonzalez
Republican candidate TX-34, 2024 — lost to Vicente Gonzalez 49-51%
biography.education: Not publicly documented in available sources
biography.background: Born in Burgos, Tamaulipas, Mexico; family moved to United States when she was six; naturalized U.S. citizen at age 14. First Mexican-born woman elected to U.S. House. Worked in cotton fields. Respiratory care practitioner by profession. Served on House Homeland Security and Agriculture Committees during her brief 2022 term. Three-time candidate for TX-34 (2022 special, 2022 general, 2024); switching back to TX-34 from TX-28 (where she had been running) after Texas Legislature redistricted in August 2025.
biography.fundraising: $1.37M raised for 2026 cycle (as of filing date)

statedPositions.quote: Secure our border to keep bad individuals out and to encourage LEGAL immigration. Illegal immigration encourages and funds human/child trafficking.
statedPositions.notes: Strong enforcement framing; she invokes her own legal immigration background as contrast. Consistent with her 2022 legislative priority (first bill was border security).

statedPositions.quote: Job creators should feel empowered, not hindered by burdensome taxes and regulations. Through smart, pro-growth policies, create an environment where small businesses can create jobs.
statedPositions.notes: Anti-regulation, pro-growth framing. No specific tax rate positions stated.

statedPositions.quote: American energy is the backbone of a strong, resilient economy. Fight for every source of reliable energy in Congress.
statedPositions.notes: All-of-the-above framing; she also stated in 2022 she 'was proud to support legislation in Congress that empowered energy producers and stopped overburdensome regulations.' No mention of climate change or clean energy transition.

statedPositions.quote: Parents should always have the right to know what their children are being taught at school... families should have the freedom to choose the education that fits their children best.
statedPositions.notes: Explicit school choice framing; also supported the Republican-led Parents Bill of Rights. Instagram posts show explicit school choice advocacy: 'School choice is about empowering parents.'

statedPositions.quote: I will always protect Social Security and Medicare, never putting the future of our older Americans in jeopardy. In Congress, I will continue working towards lower prices for care and prescriptions.
statedPositions.notes: Protects Medicare/Medicaid as programs but indicated 'no other taxpayer-funded programs are necessary.' Voted NO on Inflation Reduction Act (which included ACA subsidy extension and Medicare drug negotiation provisions). Consistent with a market-oriented but not full-abolition healthcare position.

statedPositions.quote: Unapologetically pro-life. Overturning Roe v. Wade was a dream come true for me.
statedPositions.notes: Endorsed by Texas Right to Life with explicit 'abortion ban without exception' framing. SBA Pro-Life America endorsed her. Co-sponsored Protecting Pain-Capable Unborn Children from Late-Term Abortions Act (fall 2022). 0% score from Reproductive Freedom for All (2022). No recorded softening of position.

statedPositions.quote: She believes religious liberty is at risk in the United States and deserves the highest level of protection in the law.
statedPositions.notes: Core stated value. Voted against the Respect for Marriage Act and Contraception Access bill.

keyExchanges.quote: Higher prices and more IRS audits is not an 'Inflation Reduction Act.' Anyone who thinks it's a good idea to inject $745 billion dollars into an economy already suffering from record high inflation should think again.
keyExchanges.notes: Explicit rejection of IRA's climate and healthcare provisions. Framed as economic populism (IRS audit expansion targeting ordinary people).

At debate with Vicente Gonzalez, Flores 'shrugged off' concern about mandating citizens carry passports, suggesting she'd support citizenship verification requirements that could burden border-region residents.

positionConflicts.conflict: States she will 'always protect Medicare and Medicaid' but voted No on Inflation Reduction Act (which included Medicare drug price negotiation — a cost-reduction measure that benefitted Medicare beneficiaries). Also opposed ACA subsidy extension embedded in IRA.
Positions herself as a Trump ally and MAGA Republican, but Trump endorsed her primary opponent (Eric Flores) in December 2025. She continues to campaign on her Trump-aligned record.

evidenceSummary.overallConfidence: HIGH for social issues, firearms, climate/energy, and broad economic orientation. LOW for housing, policing/sentencing, and granular healthcare cost mechanisms.
evidenceSummary.notes: Flores had only ~6 months in Congress (June–December 2022). Short record means fewer key votes than a multi-term incumbent, but her votes are unambiguous on the ones that exist: conservative across all tracked issues. Heritage Action 92% and LCV 0% are strong structural anchors. Her 2026 platform continues the same ideological direction. Key contextual note for scorer: she is running without Trump's endorsement — his backing went to rival Eric Flores — which may indicate she is more ideologically extreme even within the primary field, or at minimum lacks establishment backing.
